subject: MSA + Order Form: SLA harmonization and holiday maintenance exclusions
messages:
From: Tom Li <tom.li@avalontech.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MSA draft + order form (SLA items)

Hannah —

Thanks for sending the MSA earlier. Our procurement team reviewed the SLA section in the order form and flagged a few items we need clarity on before we can sign:

- Uptime definition: does Redwood measure uptime per-region or global? We need per-region metrics for our compliance reporting.
- Service credits: the credit cap per month looks lower than our expectation given multi-region failover costs. Is there room to increase the cap or tier the credit formula?
- Response times: P1 is listed as 30 minutes — can you confirm whether that is business hours or 24/7? We require 24/7.
- Maintenance windows: we need an exclusion list for company-wide holidays and an option for a monthly non-peak patch window that can be scheduled with 7-day notice.

Can we book 30 minutes with you and someone from legal to walk through redlines? I attached the procurement summary.

Best,
Tom
Head of Procurement, Avalon Tech
procurement@avalontech.com
Attachment: Avalon_procurement_summary_20261215.pdf (application/pdf)
From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
To: Tom Li <tom.li@avalontech.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MSA draft + order form (SLA items)

Tom —

Thanks for the clear list. Appreciate the priorities. Quick summary of where Redwood stands and next steps: 

- Uptime measurement: We measure availability per-region and report both per-region and global aggregated metrics. We can add an explicit per-region uptime clause to the order form.
- Service credits: We typically cap monthly credits at 50% of monthly committed spend for hosted customers. For strategic customers we can propose a tiered cap (e.g., 50% for first incident, 75% cumulative cap) — happy to propose language.
- Response times: Our standard P1 is 30 minutes for on-call, 24/7. We'll make that explicit (and include escalation ladder).
- Maintenance windows: We support two scheduled monthly patch windows; we can include a holiday-exclusion schedule and a 7-day notification requirement. For emergency maintenance we have different carve-outs and a maximum single-region blackout allowance.

I'm looping in Marissa (legal) and Laura (ops) to propose concrete redline language and an updated order form. Can you confirm availability for a short call tomorrow or Friday? If you prefer, we can push a redline first for you to review.

Regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
Attachment: Avalon_procurement_summary_20261215.pdf (application/pdf)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 17 Dec 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: RE: MSA draft + order form (SLA items)

Hannah / Laura —

I reviewed Tom's notes and drafted redline language for the order form and MSA. Key points I included in the redline (attached):

1) Uptime metrics: add separate definitions for region and aggregated service availability. Example clause: "Availability shall be measured per deployment region over the applicable billing period; Customer may request per-region availability reports on a monthly cadence."

2) Service credits: propose tiered credit formula and raised monthly cap for this enterprise deal: 50% cap per incident, 100% cumulative cap per billing period for qualifying outages where Redwood is the root cause. (Marked as negotiable in the draft.)

3) Response SLAs: make P1 explicit as "24/7 on-call response within 30 minutes of ticket creation" and attach the escalation ladder with names removed.

4) Maintenance and holiday exclusions: add an appendix listing US federal holidays as default exclusions, with the option for Customer to provide an alternate holiday calendar. Also added a 7-day scheduling requirement for planned monthly patch windows and stated that planned maintenance will not exceed two 4-hour windows per month per region unless otherwise agreed.

5) Emergency maintenance: clarify carve-outs and require post-incident RCA within 5 business days for emergency maintenance that impacts availability beyond the defined maintenance window.

Attached: msao-orderform-diff-annotated.txt and Redwood_SLA_LegendaryPatchProposal_20261217.xlsx

If Hannah and Laura are good with the draft, I can send to Tom with tracked changes and a short summary note. Recommend offering a 30-minute call to finalize the holiday list and the credit cap for the order form.

-Marissa
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachment: msao-orderform-diff-annotated.txt (text/plain), Redwood_SLA_LegendaryPatchProposal_20261217.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
To: Tom Li <tom.li@avalontech.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: RE: MSA draft + order form (SLA items)

Tom —

Thanks for the patience. Attached are our proposed redlines (tracked) and a short one-page summary addressing each of your bullet points. Highlights:

- Per-region availability language added.
- Tiered service credit proposal included; we recommended the 100% cumulative cap for this deal and flagged it for negotiation.
- P1 explicitly 24/7 with a 30-minute on-call response; added escalation ladder.
- Added an appendix with US federal holidays as default exclusions; we included instructions if Avalon wants to supply a different list.
- Planned maintenance: two 4-hour monthly windows per region; 7-day notice required. Emergency maintenance carve-outs and RCA within 5 business days included.

If that looks okay, Marissa will send the tracked redline to your procurement team for comment. I'm available for a 30-minute sync Friday 4:00pm PT or Monday 9:00am PT — let me know what works.

Best regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
